traits: Mouse-grey to dark grey cap, 4 to 8 cm, felted, with radial fibres that show the white flesh with age; pale, wavy margin
Notched, fragile, rather distant gills, whitish to pearl grey
Whitish stem, 3 to 8 cm, no ring
Open conifer woods, mostly under pines · autumn, into winter
safetyNote: Opinions differ. The German mycological society (2026), the Swiss controllers (2023) and French Wikipedia call it edible. A 2014 Chinese study found substances that damage muscle in mice, as in the yellow knight; a 2016 comment disputes it and a 2024 Italian study finds none and concludes it is edible. The most cautious status is kept: not recommended. The Swiss controllers say it is easily mistaken for the toxic tiger tricholoma and for some fibrecaps; ANSES records livid entolomas picked instead of « petits gris », the name it gives to the grey knight.
